source.title: Bayesian Model Selection, the Marginal Likelihood, and Generalization
source.authors: Sanae Lotfi; Pavel Izmailov; Gregory W. Benton; Micah Goldblum; A. Wilson

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own experiments showing that marginal likelihood can be negatively correlated with neural-network generalization, with the relationship changing by prior precision, calibration, and model family. This refines claims about which measured quantities track generalization; it does not test the listed memorization, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, or example-removal versions.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's reported neural architecture comparisons of marginal and conditional marginal likelihood with BMA test accuracy, including prior-precision and calibration conditions. The authors' other reported results on density estimation, Fourier models, Gaussian processes, and deep-kernel learning address marginal-likelihood alignment or hyperparameter learning, not one of V1–V8; these are summarized under fits_no_version. Cited findings from other work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether marginal likelihood predicts generalization, which is outside V1–V8. It does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness against training–test gaps (V7). Architecture width varies, but no comparison establishes widening beyond zero training error (V2).
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the main conclusion: marginal likelihood is useful for hypothesis testing but is not generally a reliable proxy for trained-model generalization. CLML improves alignment and offers practical benefits for deep-kernel hyperparameter learning, especially with limited data and transfer, while remaining susceptible to overfitting. These benefits are not universal across all kernel comparisons.
record.recipe_differences: Studies Bayesian marginal and conditional marginal likelihood as model-selection and hyperparameter criteria; it does not reproduce the original studies' training interventions or generalization measures.
record.method_sensitivity: LML correlation varies with prior precision; correlation also varies with optimized global versus layer-wise prior scales, model family (CNN versus ResNet), calibration, dataset size, and the use of BMA versus MAP metrics.

fits_no_version.finding: LML architecture rankings change from positively to negatively correlated with BMA test accuracy as prior precision decreases. CLML correlations remain positive in the reported comparisons, with calibration affecting alignment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Marginal likelihood can mis-rank trained architectures by predictive performance; conditional marginal likelihood improves alignment in the tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: In the CIFAR-10 dataset-size sweep, LML correlates positively with BMA test log-likelihood for small datasets and negatively for larger datasets; CLML remains positively correlated.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The alignment of marginal likelihood with predictive performance depends on training-set size.

fits_no_version.finding: Exact density, Fourier, and GP examples show that higher marginal likelihood can accompany poorer predictive performance. CLML addresses some underfitting mechanisms but remains susceptible to overfitting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Marginal-likelihood misalignment with generalization can arise independently of approximate inference.

fits_no_version.finding: CLML improves reported limited-data DKL regression results and several transfer comparisons. Table 4 includes a counterexample: the linear kernel reaches 75.64% accuracy with CLML versus 75.97% with LML.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CLML can improve deep-kernel hyperparameter learning in limited-data and transfer settings, but does not outperform LML for every kernel.

record.problems: Architecture comparisons use approximate inference (Kronecker Laplace or SGLD) and involve 25 architectures; individual architecture-level accuracy values are not stated in the supplied text. Several correlation values are only recoverable from figure text, and the architecture ranking correlations are not direct measurements of training–test error gaps. Calibration is examined for CNN outliers, which limits the scope of that comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows retained for CIFAR-10 architecture correlations, the SGLD CLML comparison, or the dataset-size sweep because the corresponding figure/table values are flattened and not sufficiently assignable to specific distinct conditions from the supplied text. Deep-kernel, GP, density, and Fourier results do not test V1–V8; summarized under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Matched random-label and natural-label training, memorization capacity, and held-out accuracy.
Test-error changes from widening beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under comparable tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels apply because none of V1–V8 is tested. Negative correlation signs lost in the flattened figures are supported by the accompanying prose; coefficient assignments above follow Appendix F, Figure 12. Generic discussion of curvature and PAC-Bayes bounds does not test V7.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test-error behavior when widening beyond interpolation.
CNN versus fully connected generalization and the role of local connectivity.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Effect of removing memorized examples on test accuracy.

rows.subject: CNNs
rows.operation_detail: Measured correlation of LML and BMA test accuracy after optimizing one global prior precision.
rows.measure: Spearman’s ρ between LML ranking and BMA test accuracy ranking
rows.note: Authors state that the correlation remains negative for CNN models when only a global prior precision is optimized; the figure's ρ is reported as 0.43 without clarified sign in the flattened display.
rows.check: Subject and value are mismatched. Figures 5(c) and 20 report 0.705 across CNNs and ResNets with optimized global precision. The text states that the CNN-only correlation is negative but supplies no recoverable CNN-only coefficient; positive 0.43 is unsupported.

rows.check: The pooled CNN/ResNet correlation 0.877 agrees with Figures 5(c) and 20. It measures LML alignment, not a listed claim.
